instructions: Presentations.AI for Business creates finished, designed slide decks from a prompt, pasted text or an outline, exports them as PPTX, PDF or slide images, and manages the user's decks. Generating a deck spends workspace credits, so create one only when the user asks. Generation runs in the background and takes a few minutes. Share a deck by public link, or send feedback, only when the user asks. Pass ids from earlier results exactly as returned.

tools.name: whoami
tools.title: Check account and credits
tools.description:
Show the connected account's email, workspace, role, plan, and credit balance.

Use it when the user asks which account is connected, its plan, or its credits left.

plan.description: The workspace's plan; it decides which features are available.

outputSchema.description: The connected account, its workspace, role and plan, and the credit balance.

tools.name: create_presentation
tools.title: Create presentation
tools.description:
Create a finished, designed presentation from a prompt, text, or an outline.

Use it when the user asks for a presentation, deck, slides, a pitch, or a
PowerPoint. The deck is saved in the user's Presentations.AI workspace and can
be exported as PPTX, PDF or slide images, or shared by link.

`deck` takes e.g. `prompt`, `sources` (`{"type": "text", "content": ...}`, or
`{"type": "file", "file_id": ...}` for a file already uploaded to the user's Presentations.AI workspace),
`slide_count`, `audience`, `level_of_detail`, `deck_purpose`,
`brand_kit_id` (find one with `search_brand_kits`), or an edited `outline` from
`create_outline`.
Retrying an identical call returns the same deck; pass a new `request_id` to
generate another copy.

Generation spends credits and takes a few minutes in the background: poll
`task_id` with `get_task`, then fetch the file with `get_export`, or a public
link with `share_deck` when the user asks for one.

deck.description: The presentation to create; needs a `deck_title`, `prompt`, `sources` or `outline`.

prompt.description: Topic and instructions for the presentation, or pasted content to build from. Cannot be combined with `outline`.

type.description: `text`: Inline factual source material supplied directly in the request. `file`: A file already uploaded to the user's Presentations.AI workspace.

content.description: Factual material to build from; all text sources together are capped at 200,000 characters. Required when `type` is `text`. Leave it out when `type` is `file`.

file_id.description: The id of a file already uploaded to the user's Presentations.AI workspace; its text must have finished extracting, or the call is refused. Required when `type` is `file`. Leave it out when `type` is `text`.

sources.description: Inline text, or files already uploaded to the user's Presentations.AI workspace. Cannot be combined with `outline`.

name.description: Deck name shown in the workspace. Omitted: `deck_title`, else the outline's `documentTitle`, else the title generated with the outline, else "Untitled Presentation".

visibility.description: Who can open the deck. `PROJECT` requires `project_id`.

project_id.description: Project to create the deck in. Required for `PROJECT` visibility; a connection limited to one project must pass that project.

deck_title.description: Requested presentation title. Alone it is enough to generate from; it also names the deck when `name` is omitted.

outline.description: The `outline` object from `create_outline`, edited as needed. Skips outline generation; cannot be combined with `prompt` or sources.

documentTitle.description: Presentation title; names the deck when no `name` or `deck_title` is given.

hook.description: The deck's opening angle in a sentence or two.

researchSummary.description: Summary of the research the outline draws on.

contentLanguage.description: Language the outline is written in, as an English name.

footerText.description: One-line footer for the whole deck.

imagePrompt.description: Prompt for the generated cover image.

contentMode.description: `retain` or `condense` when the outline mirrors supplied content; layouts then keep its structure instead of reshaping it.

companyName.description: Company the deck is about: the requested `company`, else one detected from the topic.

audienceQuestions.description: Questions the audience arrives with, which the deck answers.

heading.description: Slide title; may wrap one key span in `**bold**`.

subheading.description: Optional subtitle; on the cover it is the deck subtitle.

description.description: Plain-text slide content; the content source when `graphics` is absent.

category.description: Fallback for `useCase` when that is absent.

useCase.description: 2-4 word slide-purpose label shown above the title; `Cover` and `Section Break` mark those slide kinds.

visualComposition.description: Ordered graphic types used to pick the layout, starting with `titleandsubtitle`; a comma-separated string is also accepted.

graphics.description: The slide's charts, tables, lists and other body graphics, in reading order. Keep these as `create_outline` returned them; edit their text if needed.

imageQuery.description: Stock-photo search caption describing what the photo shows.

sources.description: Publishers of the figures on this slide. Keep these as `create_outline` returned them; edit their text if needed.

confidence.description: `high`, `medium` or `low`: how firmly the slide's figures are sourced.

knowledge.description: Figures the outline states from general knowledge, each with the source it names. Keep these as `create_outline` returned them; edit their text if needed.

company.description: Company the deck is about; seeds research and the outline's `companyName` instead of inferring it from the prompt.

creator_role.description: Author's job title; sets background tone and research budget. Omitted: the connected user's profile role.

model.description: Generation model tier, case-insensitive. A tier above the workspace plan's is refused.

language.description: Output language as an English name (e.g. `French`); `auto` follows the language of the prompt and sources.

slide_count.description: Slides including the cover, each number 1-50: `N` exact, `N-M` a range, `N+` at least N, `auto` or omitted lets Presentations.AI decide. `1` yields one summary slide with no cover.

level_of_detail.description:
Text density per content item, case-insensitive. Omitted: adapted to the topic and content.

BRIEF: label plus at most a short line. STANDARD: one sentence. DETAILED: 1-2
sentences. VERY_DETAILED: 2-3 sentences.

insider_content.description: Private background facts about your organisation. Used where a slide calls for them, never cited; counts toward the plan content limit.

export_format.description: Format of the artifact exported when generation completes.

audience.description: Who the deck is for. Omitted: inferred from the prompt and sources, never asked back.

deck_purpose.description: Purpose id from the deck purpose taxonomy: pitch, sales, marketing, strategy, report, training, teaching, coursework, product, research, security, general.

brand_kit_id.description: Style the deck as a brand: an `id` from `search_brand_kits`. Omitted: no brand kit.

deep_search.description: Consultant-grade research and exhibit slides (paid plans; doubles the deck's per-slide credits). Not applicable to an authored outline.

budget_tier.description: Quality tier: `lite`, `standard` (default) or `premium`, each billed at its own per-slide rate. It never asks questions, at any tier.

missing_data.description: A figure only you hold that nobody gave: `placeholder` leaves a `[DATA NEEDED: …]` marker; `estimate` writes a plausible estimate (recorded as one in the outline's figure check). Omitted: taken from what the prompt asks for ("use only my numbers" leaves markers), else `estimate`.

fidelity.description: How source material is used: `retain` keeps its slides, `condense` keeps its sections and tightens them, `context` builds a new deck from it. Omitted: picked from the request and the material.

narrative.description: Narrative arc the storyline follows (e.g. `answer_first`, `what_why_how`). Omitted: the usual arc for the purpose and audience.

delivery.description: How the deck is shown: `stage` (a big screen), `meeting`, `video` (a call), `read` (sent and read alone) or `print`. Sets the words per slide.

use_case.description: Use case id from the create flow's list; it sets the deck's writing style, audience and story arc.

speaker_notes.description: Write presenter talking points for every slide.

company_domain.description: The company's web domain (e.g. `example.com`); with `company`, seeds research and the brand lookup.

graphic_types.description: Allow-list of body graphics the deck may use (e.g. `table`, `list`, `diagram`); anything else is redrawn as the closest allowed type.

diagram_subtypes.description: Allow-list of diagram shapes (e.g. `process`, `cycle`) when `diagram` is allowed.

request_id.description: Optional idempotency key. Omitted: retrying an identical request returns the same deck; after a FAILED run, or once that deck is deleted, it starts a new one.

status.description: Lifecycle state of an async task: CREATED (queued), RUNNING, then COMPLETED or FAILED.

deck_url.description: Opens the deck in the PresentationsAI app; requires signing in as a member with access. Not a public link: use `share_deck` for one.

outputSchema.description: A dispatched deck-generation run: the new deck, its task handle, and app link.

tools.name: get_task
tools.title: Check generation status
tools.description:
Status of a background task, such as a presentation generation.

Waits up to `wait_time` seconds (at most 50) until the task is COMPLETED
or FAILED, then returns its latest status. Once a generation is COMPLETED, `get_export`
returns its file.

wait_time.description: Seconds to wait for the task to finish, at most 50; 0 returns at once. Some clients always get an immediate answer.

kind.description: What the task does, e.g. deck generation.

status.description: Lifecycle state of an async task: CREATED (queued), RUNNING, then COMPLETED or FAILED.

tools.name: get_export
tools.title: Get download link
tools.description:
Get a short-lived download link for the latest file the user exported from this deck.

Only the connected user's own exports count; it fails if they have none for it yet.

deck_id.description: The deck's id, from create_presentation or list_decks.

format.description: Export artifact format: PPTX, PDF, or IMAGE (a ZIP with one image per slide).

download_url.description: Anonymous download link; it expires after 15 minutes, so call `get_export` again for a fresh one.

outputSchema.description: A produced export artifact with a short-lived, anonymous download URL.

tools.name: share_deck
tools.title: Share deck by public link
tools.description:
Get or create the deck's public share link and return the URL.

Anyone with the link can open the deck, so use it only when the user asks for a
link or to share the deck. Reuses the existing link so the URL is stable; pass
rotate=true to mint a fresh one (the previous URL stops working).

deck_id.description: The deck's id, from create_presentation or list_decks.

rotate.description: true replaces the existing public link; the old link stops working.

share_url.description: Public view link: opens the deck without signing in, subject to the link's password or expiry.

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.title: Send feedback
tools.description:
Send a note about this connector to Presentations.AI.

Only when the user asks to, or approves after seeing the exact message. It changes
nothing in the workspace and costs no credits.

message.description: The note exactly as the user approved it. Leave out the content of their documents and decks.

tool.description: The tool the feedback is about.

outputSchema.description: Acknowledgement that the feedback was stored.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.title: List projects
tools.description:
List projects, or folders with `kind=FOLDER`; `parent_id` lists one project's or folder's children.

`top_level=true` lists only the user's top level: items with no parent, or whose parent they cannot open. It can't be combined with `parent_id`. A connection limited to one project sees that project and the folders below it.

kind.description: What a row is: a project or a plain folder.

parent_id.title: Parent Id
parent_id.description: Only the children of this project or folder.

top_level.title: Top Level
top_level.description: Only your top level: no parent, or one you cannot open. Not with `parent_id`.

total.description: Items matching the filters across all pages.
total.title: Total

tools.name: search_brand_kits
tools.title: Find brand kits
tools.description:
Search the brand kits you can style a deck with.

Use a result's `id` as `brand_kit_id` when creating a deck. Includes published brands, your
workspace's kits and your own unshared kits. A brand limited to approved email domains appears
only when your verified email domain is one of them.

access.title: KitAccess
access.description: Why you can see it. PUBLIC: open to everyone. DOMAIN: limited to approved email domains, and yours is one. WORKSPACE: your workspace's kit. OWNER: your own kit.

tools.name: create_outline
tools.title: Draft outline
tools.description: Draft a slide-by-slide outline from a prompt or the user's files, without creating a deck. Edit it and pass it as `deck.outline` to `create_presentation`. Each outline charges 10 credits per slide, once, when it is ready, and fails when the workspace has too few credits. A repeat call drafts and charges again unless it sends the same `request_id`, which is then refused without a second charge.
